messages.subject: [GSoC-R] 24 hours left
messages.body_plain:
We now have only a little more than 24 hours left to finalize student
proposals.

I have read all the proposals as of yesterday evening, and will be
going through the new ones today.

I see that many mentors are commenting on proposals, which is good.

Students, you need to respond to the concerns raises by mentors for
your project or by other R mentors.  Google has explicitly instructed
us to weight this in our deliberations after the application period
closes.

Google's deadlines are firm, and there are no exceptions.  Only
complete applications following the R application template will be
considered for a slot request.

Please contact Toby or me as soon as possible if you need assistance
with something.

Regards,

Brian

messages.subject: [R-GSoC] Next Steps
messages.body_plain:
Student Applications are now closed.  I believe R received more high
quality applications this year than in any previous year.  Some
projects received as many as 6 applications, so this will be a
competitive and difficult year to choose winners.

Thank you all for participating.

Now to go over next steps.  Both Students and Mentors have things to
do.  Failure to complete these tasks will result in not getting a slot.

Students:
You may not, under any circumstances, ask about whether you have been
accepted, or are likely to be accepted to GSoC this year.  Google will
inform all of the thousands of students who applied to GSoC at the same
time, and announce those who have slots on the GSoC website.

Google will be reviewing your proof of enrollment.  In many cases, they
will be asking you to update it to provide proof of current enrollment
or other eligibility issues for GSoC.  Pay close attention to these
requests, and respond as quickly as possible.  Google does not share
these requests with org admins (Toby and me) or Mentors.  If you do not
have updated or accepted final proof or enrollment on file by Google's
deadline (I believe Apr 15th), you will not be eligible to receive a
slot.

Mentors:
Some mentors have not accepted their invitations.  If you're having
trouble, please contact Toby or me immediately, and we'll try to help
you.  If we do not have all listed mentors in the Google system by slot
assignment time, with feedback entered as below, your project idea will
not get a slot.

You must not communicate with students about acceptance or rejection.
Nothing is Final till May and the Google announcement.

Toby and I will be doing a first review of submitted applications.  We
will be commenting on proposals and contacting mentors individually for
feedback where necessary.  According to Google guidelines, discussion
about student proposals should happen in the comment section of the
proposal wherever possible (Students don't see this section).

We also need all R Project Mentors to do a few things on the Google
Summer of Code system as soon as possible:

1> We need you to select 'Want to Mentor' on an application for a
project where you are listed as a mentor, or on the strongest
application for the project where there are multiple applications for a
single project.

2> We also need you to comment on *all* applications for projects where
you are listed as a mentor in the 'Comment on this Proposal' section at
the bottom of the proposal page.  Please provide a succinct summary of
your feelings on the application.  These comments are visible to other
R mentors only, not to the students.  We want all mentors to comment on
all proposals for a project you are a listed mentor for.

3> We *want*, but cannot require, that you comment on other student
applications for proposed projects that you will not be mentoring this
summer.  Please comment on projects where you have some expertise.
Google used to require all mentors to vote on applications, but that
was removed from the process last year.  Your input is still very
valuable to Toby and me as we review applications and make slot
requests.

Slot request to Google will happen no later than April 17th, per the
Google Deadline.  You will see slot request numbers start to show up as
early as today, and preliminary starring of high quality proposals.
None of these are final.  Feel free to contact Toby and me off-list
with questions or concerns.  Input on applications should go in the
'Comment on This Proposal' section, as described above.

April 19th-24th Toby and I will communicate with mentors and allocate
the slots we've received from Google.

On May 4th, accepted projects will be announced by Google.

Between April 3rd and May 4th, Google prohibits mentors and
organizations from telling students whether or not their proposal has
been accepted.  Students, please don't ask.  Mentors, you must not
tell.  Google takes a very dim view of breaking this rule.

As always, please do not hesitate to contact me or Toby with any
questions or concerns.

Regards,

Brian

--
Brian G. Peterson
http://braverock.com/brian/
Ph: 773-459-4973
IM: bgpbraverock

messages.subject: [GSoC-R] Mentors: We need your input NOW!
messages.subject_clean: [GSoC-R] Mentors: We need your input NOW!
messages.body_plain:
Mentors:

We *really* need you to comment on your student proposals.  We have a
very large number of high quality proposals, and need to make slot
requests from Google.

We really need you to help Toby and me by commenting on the strengths
and weaknesses of each proposal for one of your project ideas.

Any proposal that does not have (detailed, positive) comments from at
least two of the proposed project mentors isn't going to get a slot.

Google also requires you to select 'Want to Mentor' for the proposal.
We need at least two mentors to (provisionally) slot the project.

Google's deadline is coming up, and I will err on the side of
requesting fewer slots if we don't have input.  Please get your initial
input into the summerofcode system this weekend and make sure you've
selected 'Want to Mentor' if you have a "truly excellent" proposal
(those are Google's words, not mine).

If you have additional questions for the students, you are encouraged
to continue communicating with the student to work them out.  Please
don't telegraph strong/weak proposal feelings, and you must not promise
or hint at acceptance rejection (it is against Google program rules, as
I've previously shared).

We are refining the min/max slot request numbers daily as we review
proposals and get more feedback from mentors.  We are starting to
provisionally star strong proposals with clear mentor support.  Your
input is critical over the next several days for us to make a well-
informed request to Google.  Please help us out.

Students:

As just described above, you may receive communication from mentors on
your proposals.  If you do, please respond as quickly as possible.  The
clock is ticking to slot requests to Google, and we are instructed to
take student communication into account in granting slots once we've
received a slot allocation from Google.

As always, please reach out to Toby or me if you have any questions or
concerns.

Regards,

Brian

--
Brian G. Peterson

Congratulations, R project for statistical computing has been granted 37 project slots for GSoC 2017.

It is now time to choose the student proposals you want to have as projects for your organization. You must assign at least one mentor when you select a student.

Your organization is not required to use all of the slots allocated. Please note that you cannot give your unused slots to other organizations.

We have a fixed number of student project slots and have distributed them across all of the accepted organizations. If you were hoping for more student slots this year -- we are sorry -- no additional slots will be allocated.

You may wish to re-review the slot allocation guidelines <https://developers.google.com/open-source/gsoc/help/slot-allocation> for information on student selection criteria and handling conflicts.

If you have any questions about this process, please ask about it on the Mentors' list or email gsoc-s...@google.com.

For any questions, please contact gsoc-s...@google.com. Replies to this message go to an unmonitored mailbox.

messages.subject: 3 hours to next Google deadline
messages.body_plain:
Mentors:

At this point, *I* believe all projects that have been approved by the
R mentor community and passed our acceptance criteria are marked as
accepted in the Google Summer of Code administrative system.

I hope that all of the mentors have looked at your preferred projects
and made sure that things are as you expect them. correct comments,
correct students, correct outcomes.  If there are any issues, Toby and
I need to know ASAP off-list so that we can correct them.

You should be able to see everything from your dashboard:

Students:

I know the waiting is hard on you, and you still have a week and a half
to go until you know whether you've been accepted.  I have a request to
all prospective R GSoC students. Every year, we lose a slot or two the
week after student acceptance because a student tells us *after* being
accepted that they won't be able to do the project. If you have new
conflicts, or some other internship you plan to accept, or some other
reason that would force you to withdraw from the program, please let us
know *before* the student acceptance announcements.  Until May 4th, and
the official announcements, we have a little latitude to accept a
different project if a student withdraws.  Please, if this applies to
you, tell us as soon as possible, after the final acceptance deadline
today, but before the student acceptance announcements next week.  That
way your disclosure can't change our acceptance status, but it could
let you help another student take a slot that would otherwise be
forfeited.

As always, if you have any questions or concerns, please feel free to
let Toby or me know immediately.

Regards,

Brian

--
Brian G. Peterson
